newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MORE THAN JUST NORTH-EAST PRIDE AT STAKE NOW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MORE THAN JUST NORTH-EAST PRIDE AT STAKE NOW.

text.p: Once, all that really mattered in England's North-East derbies was local pride because Newcastle, Middlesbrough or Sunderland had no real chance of winning any silverware.

But all that has changed now and when assorted Brazilians, French, Italian and Colombian players run out in the black-and-white stripes of Newcastle and the red shirts of Middlesbrough for Sunday's premier league match, far more will be at stake than ever before.
Newcastle go into the game second in the table, eager to bounce back from last week's shock 2-0 league defeat at Leicester, while Middlesbrough will be looking for their first win since September 14.

The stakes are higher now because, between them, Newcastle manager Kevin Keegan and Middlesbrough's Bryan Robson have spent 80 million pounds ($130 million) assembling sides good enough to challenge for trophies.
And, while local pride is still at stake on Sunday, the quest for three league points is far more important to the clubs.

Although Newcastle came back from the Leicester defeat to score an impressive 4-0 win over Ferencvaros in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday, they are likely to change their line-up and tactics for Sunday's match and return to the formation which crushed Manchester United two weeks ago.

Keegan played with a three-man defence of Darren Peacock, Philippe Albert and Robbie Elliott against Ferencvaros but is likely to revert to a 4-4-2 formation for Sunday's match and must decide whether Steve Watson or Warren Barton, back in favour after six months on the sidelines, plays at right back and whether fit-again John Beresford will replace Elliott on the left.
Beresford will make his 150th appearance for Newcastle if he does play but Elliott played well against the Hungarians and would be disappointed to be left out.

One man definitely missing is world record signing Alan Shearer, who is recovering from groin surgery. But there was encouraging news for Keegan -- and England boss Glenn Hoddle -- when Shearer said he hoped to be fit to play against Middlesbrough when the sides meet again in the fourth round of the League Cup on November 27.

In Shearer's absence, Colombian Faustino Asprilla, who scored twice against Ferencvaros and had his best game for Newcastle since joining them last January, should keep his place up front alongside Les Ferdinand and French winger David Ginola, Tuesday's other scorers.
Middlesbrough make the short trip to Newcastle looking for their first league win since a 2-1 victory at Everton on September 14.

If Middlesbrough are to get anything out of the match, Brazilian Emerson will have to win the midfield battle against Newcastle's David Batty, thus relieving some of the pressure on a defence which has leaked 18 goals already this season, the joint-worst in the division.
Assistant manager Viv Anderson is hopeful, however, that Middlesbrough turned the corner last week when they drew 0-0 with Wimbledon.
"There were signs last week we were getting it right at the back," he said on Friday. "And I was very pleased our defence gave nothing away against Wimbledon, who had won their last seven matches."
Skipper Nigel Pearson, who suffered concussion against Wimbledon, has made a full recovery and is expected to play in an unchanged team.

Even though he has spent some 25 million pounds ($40 million) on his squad he knows his defence needs strengthening and, following the 5.7 million pounds ($9.3 million) sale of Nicky Barmby to Everton this week, he is not short of cash.
Rangers full back David Robertson is one target and reports from Middlesbrough suggest he could move south next week.

With both teams committed to attacking football against suspect defences, with Middlesbrough's Fabrizio Ravanelli being the top scorer in the premier league and with a passionate, capacity crowd behind them, the 99th Tyne-Tees cup and league derby looks set to produce a thrilling high-scoring affair.
Teams:

Newcastle (from): 1-Pavel Srnicek; 2-Warren Barton, 19-Steve Watson, 5-Darren Peacock, 27-Philippe Albert, 26-Robbie Elliott, 3-John Beresford, 4-David Batty, 7-Robert Lee, 8-Peter Beardsley, 18-Keith Gillespie, 14-David Ginola, 10-Les Ferdinand, 11-Faustino Asprilla, 28-Paul Kitson, 20-Lee Clark

Middlesbrough (from): 13-Gary Walsh, 1-Alan Miller; 2-Neil Cox, 5-Nigel Pearson, 4-Steve Vickers, 6-Emerson, 8-Robbie Mustoe, 9-Mikkel Beck, 20-Phil Stamp, 10-Juninho, 11-Fabrizio Ravanelli, 14-Curtis Fleming, 3-Derek Whyte, 15-Phil Whelan
